summary.headline: Epigral posted record Q4 FY26 revenue of INR736 crore (+22% QoQ) and 23% EBITDA margin; management guides FY27 volume growth of 10-12%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR736 crore, up 22% QoQ on 15% volume growth, with plant utilisation above 80% after the major caustic soda maintenance ended in Q3. EBITDA rose 64% QoQ to INR169 crore, margin 23%, and PAT was INR82 crore (11% margin). FY26 revenue fell 1% to INR2,542 crore on a ~4% volume decline; reported PAT of INR330 crore includes an INR81 crore one-time deferred tax benefit, so underlying PAT was INR252 crore versus INR357 crore. Management said the war-driven price spike mostly lands in Q1 FY27, not Q4, and the company is targeting 10-12% volume growth in FY27.

segments.name: Derivatives and specialty business
segments.commentary: Contributed 54% of Q4 FY26 revenue versus 52% in Q3. Products include ECH, CPVC, chloromethanes and hydrogen peroxide per the Q&A.

segments.name: Chlor-alkali (caustic soda)
segments.commentary: Utilisation rose from roughly 67-70% in the first half of FY26 to about 78-85% after mid-November 2025, following the once-in-eight-years major maintenance finished in Q3. Q4 ECU was about INR30,000.

segments.name: Chlorotoluene
segments.commentary: Commissioned in March 2025; still in customer approvals, with volumes starting to ramp. Plant utilisation was minimal in FY26; management expects about 40% in FY27 and 70-75% optimum in FY28. Mainly serves agrochemical and pharma customers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth targeted at 10-12%, which management says drives value growth; it declined to guide on EBITDA margin beyond saying Q4 levels would be maintained.
War-driven raw material and product price increases expected to show mainly in Q1 FY27; caustic soda prices rose 30-35% after the war but have cooled to an ECU of about INR37,000 currently.
ECH and CPVC capacity doubling expected to commission in Q2 FY27; ramp-up from about 15-20% utilisation, with optimum around 75% for CPVC and 80% for ECH in FY28.
Chlorine captive consumption to rise from about 75% to 90-95% (including pipeline customers) by FY28 once ECH and CPVC run at optimum.
Management expects it will take 4-5 months for realisations to normalise even after the conflict pauses; April 2026 volumes were soft, with growth expected to pick up from May.
New greenfield project under evaluation; management says it will be announced in calendar 2026, with the company stating it wants consistent growth beyond FY29-FY30.
Wind-solar addition of about 19.5 MW expected to lift renewable share of power from 8-9% to around 15% of requirement once commissioned.
capex_capacity: ECH and CPVC capacity expansion on track and within budget; commissioning expected in Q2 FY27, roughly doubling capacity per the Q&A.
Chlorotoluene plant commissioned March 2025; FY27 expected to bring a sizeable contribution, with optimum utilisation of 70-75% in FY28.
Capital work in progress stood at INR451 crore at FY26 end.
Caustic soda utilisation after the Q3 maintenance: about 78-85%; company-wide utilisation above 80% in Q4 FY26.
No plans to add caustic soda capacity currently, although management said it may do so if required.
Wind-solar addition of about 19.5 MW planned.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 volume growth of 15% QoQ; demand picked up from mid-November 2025 after the monsoon ended, with CPVC demand recovering alongside.
Management said about 60% of the product basket goes into essential applications where demand holds at elevated prices, while about 40% faces demand restriction from higher prices.
Q4 benefited little from the war price spike because monthly contracts were priced at the start of March; the price increase is expected to show in Q1 FY27.
CPVC prices track PVC prices, which management described as highly volatile; no specific price trend was given.
Exports are only about 4-5% of sales, mainly to Europe.
Chlorotoluene orders rose from January 2026 but softened during the war; the company expects volume growth from May.
Chloromethanes and other products rose in line with raw material prices; management cited about 50% for chloromethanes in one answer.

qa_highlights.question: What was the realised ECU in Q4 and what is the current trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 ECU was about INR30,000/t. Caustic prices rose 30-35% after the war and have since cooled, with the current ECU around INR37,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: What went wrong in the first nine months and what are the tailwinds now?
qa_highlights.answer: The planned caustic maintenance (once every eight years) ran until October, and a prolonged monsoon plus PVC volatility hit CPVC demand. Utilisation rose from 67-70% to 78-85% after November.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 the new normal and what is FY27 volume guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 levels are the operating baseline and that it is targeting 10-12% volume growth in FY27, with value growth from higher-value products. It declined to give an EBITDA peak target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of power comes from renewables and how does this compare with industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Wind-solar is 8-9% of power consumption, rising to about 15% after the 19.5 MW addition. Management did not have the industry figure but said adoption is low at present.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 revenue beat FY26 and will EBITDA margin hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 volume growth to lift value, but it did not guide on revenue growth percentage or EBITDA margin beyond maintaining the current range.

qa_highlights.question: Why was finance cost high at INR72 crore versus guidance of INR45-50 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase was a mark-to-market impact on a foreign-currency loan with an FX swap, driven by the rupee's depreciation beyond its historical 2-3% a year. Management said finance is looking at mitigation.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: higher raw material and energy costs (energy up ~15%) and disrupted shipping could dampen demand for the ~40% of the basket that is price-sensitive.
Price normalisation: management expects realisations to take 4-5 months to settle, so Q1 FY27 pricing and volume may swing.
Monsoon and El Nino risk: FY26 volume decline was partly due to weak monsoon demand for CPVC and ECH.
Ramp-up risk: ECH and CPVC commissioning in Q2 FY27 with slow initial utilisation (15-20%); chlorotoluene volumes are still minimal.
Forex exposure: the rupee's depreciation caused mark-to-market finance cost of about INR72 crore; a 2-3% move is seen as manageable.
Greenfield project announcement expected in 2026, with details still under evaluation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the volume recovery and FY27 growth, but cautious and evasive on pricing, margins and any numbers beyond volume guidance, repeatedly citing war uncertainty. Management declined to give revenue growth, EBITDA margin, chlorotoluene utilisation and realisation figures on the call.
key_quotes: So that's where you can say Quarter 4, I mean, even from mid of November, we were running at optimum for both, I mean, the whole plant put together.
So to put it short, the price increase because of war will be majorly reflected in Q1 and not in Q4.
I would avoid giving any number, but in terms of volume growth, we are targeting around 10% to 12% of volume growth from here on.
